questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman had a thrombotic stroke and was given a high dose of Alteplase by a newly joined resident in the cardiology department. The antidote for its overdose is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Epsilon amino caproic acid
  • Epsilon amino-caproic acid(EACA) and Tranexamic acid are the drugs that inhibit plasminogen activation and dissolution of the clot
  • so they are used in bleeding conditions like menorrhagia, epistaxis, subarachnoid and GI hemorrhage Abruptio placentae, PPH, and menorrhagia
  • Epsilon amino-caproic acid(EACA) and Tranexamic acid are used in fibrinolytic overdose


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 676

questions.stem: ADP receptor antagonists are used as Antiplatelet drugs in myocardial infarction. Which of the following drugs reversibly block P2Y12?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ticagrelor

Is an orally active, reversible inhibitor of the P2Y12 receptor, it can be stopped 1 day before surgery.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old male patient was put on Prasugrel after acute coronary syndrome and managed with percutaneous coronary intervention. He also has moderate renal failure and liver impairment. After 1 month he presents with serious bleeding episodes. What is the next appropriate step among the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Reduce the dose of Prasugrel, as the patient has renal failure

options.label: D
options.text: Reduce the dose of Prasugrel, as the patient has a liver impairment

questions.solutionHtml:
Platelet transfusion may be beneficial
  • Prasugrel
  • No dose adjustment is required in patients with hepatic or renal impairment.
  • If patients present with serious bleeding, platelet transfusion may be beneficial
  • Prasugrel has been reported to cause thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
  • Adding aspirin in bleeding episodes will still worsen bleeding


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 597

questions.stem: Inhibition of thromboxane synthesis by aspirin in platelets lasts for 5-7 days because:

options.label: A
options.text: Aspirin persists in the body for 5-7 days

options.label: B
options.text: Aspirin-induced depletion of arachidonic acid lasts 5-7 days

options.label: C
options.text: Regeneration of aspirin-inhibited cyclooxygenase takes 5-7 days

options.label: D
options.text: Platelets cannot generate fresh thromboxane synthetase and their turnover time is 5-7 days

questions.answerText: Platelets cannot generate fresh thromboxane synthetase and their turnover time is 5-7 days
questions.solutionHtml:
Platelets cannot generate fresh thromboxane synthetase and their turnover time is 5-7 days

questions.stem: An old woman is required to receive 4 cycles of cancer chemotherapy. After her first cycle, she developed chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. Then in the next cycle, it would be appropriate to give this patient:
questions.solutionHtml:
Oprelvekin( IL-11)

Oprelvekin acts like a megakaryocyte colony-stimulating factor and can be used to treat and prevent chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia.
